partner_result_applied.scope: For any nonzero original-coordinate diagonal coefficient a_ll, the full coupled characteristic function obeys ||phi_Q||_3^3 <= 16*pi/|a_ll|.

new_claim.statement: For disjoint physical coordinate sets I,J with |I|=|J|=k and invertible C=A[I,J], arbitrary independent marginal densities <=1 and arbitrary remaining matrix entries satisfy |phi_Q(t)|<=min(1,pi^(k/2)|det C|^(-1/2)|t|^(-k/2)). For k>=3, Q has a bounded continuous density with ||p_Q||_infinity<=k/(k-2)|det C|^(-1/k).
new_claim.proof_mechanism: Exact Plancherel in the random linear coefficient beta after conditioning: integral |F_t(beta)|^2 d beta <=(2*pi)^k |t|^-k; beta=2CX_J+shift has density <=2^-k|det C|^-1.

partner_combination: For k=3, D=|det A[I,J]| and nonzero diagonal a, Holder on low frequencies using account02/B01 plus the new t^-3/2 tail gives ||p_Q||_infinity <= 7*2^(-1/7)*3^(-3/7)|a|^(-1/7)D^(-2/7) <3.960 |a|^(-1/7)D^(-2/7).
aggregated_corollary: For a physical triple I with C=A[I,I^c], rank C=3 and s_I=sqrt(det(CC^T)), the bounded-density orthogonal-projection theorem plus the same Plancherel step yields ||p_Q||_infinity<=3*C_RV*s_I^(-1/3), and s_I^2 is the sum of squared disjoint 3x3 cross minors by Cauchy-Binet.
unresolved_implication: From the sole spectral hypothesis (at least three |eigenvalues|>=1), prove a dimension-free dichotomy: some physical triple has cross-volume s_I>=c>0, or A has a quantitatively controlled localized/separable structure already covered by a source-valid theorem.
next_step: Use A[I,I^c]A[I,I^c]^T=(A^2)[I,I]-A[I,I]^2 and exterior-power mass to attack the dichotomy. Diagonal matrices force a real second branch, so cross-volume alone cannot be universal.
